strengths: Well-motivated formulation addressing complementary limitations of weight-level RL and feed-forward prompt refinement through closed-loop latent feedback

Comprehensive experimental validation spanning single/composite rewards, multiple model architectures (SD1.5, SDXL, SDXL-turbo, FLUX.1-dev, SD3.5), with consistent improvements across ImageReward, HPSv2, and aesthetic metrics
Strong practical properties: orthogonality with existing alignment methods, plug-and-play composability, zero-shot generalization to unseen models without retraining
Thorough ablation studies validating each component (Table 3, Fig. 6) and insightful secondary analyses (prompt evolution, semantic drift quantification, training stability)
Excellent reproducibility with detailed algorithms, implementation hyperparameters, prompting templates, and minimal inference overhead (18s/image vs 15s baseline on A100)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—primarily an engineering combination of existing techniques (MLLM prompt refinement + GRPO training) in closed-loop configuration rather than fundamental methodological innovation

Overclaimed 'structural equivalence' to Diffusion RL; prompts are indirect control signals with complex dynamics, not direct distribution sampling—equivalence framing is misleading despite acknowledged 'structural correspondence'

Insufficient reward hacking resistance analysis: qualitative improvements observed but no systematic evaluation, adversarial robustness testing, or formal analysis of whether buffering effect is due to prompt-level indirection

Sparse refinement strategy lacks principled justification (why 5 steps? why even spacing?) and computational overhead of 3s MLLM inference per image is non-trivial for deployment despite being called 'negligible'
No failure case analysis or discussion of method limitations; qualitative results appear cherry-picked; behavior with adversarial/misaligned reward functions unexplored

Generalization claims need nuance—zero-shot transfer tested only on related Stable Diffusion variants and SNR-based timestep conversion for flow-matching suggests potential brittleness for divergent architectures
Missing statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing despite stochastic sampling; single evaluation runs implied; sample sizes for generalization unspecified
Semantic drift quantification questionable—LLM-based concept extraction may miss subtle drift, and Table 5 shows substantial prompt evolution warranting discussion of acceptable modification bounds
